section_1.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: Conditional Probability
section_1.content: Briefly define Conditional Probability P(A|B) as focusing on a reduced sample space. Use a Venn diagram to visually show the 'slice' of A inside B.
section_1.example: Visualizing a grid of 100 people; highlighting only those who own a dog (B) and then identifying the subset who also own a cat (A).

section_2.title: The Concept of Independence
section_2.content: Explain that events A and B are independent if P(A|B) = P(A). Visually demonstrate this as 'the presence of B does not change the ratio of A in the universe'.
section_2.example: Flipping a coin twice: The result of the first flip does not change the 50/50 probability distribution of the second flip.

section_3.title: Introducing Bayes' Theorem
section_3.content: Introduce the theorem as a mechanism to update beliefs (Posterior) based on new evidence (Likelihood). Use a 'Probability Tree' animation showing the flow from Prior to Posterior.
section_3.example: A 'Medical Detective' scenario: Given a positive test result (Evidence), what is the actual probability of having the disease (Posterior)?

section_4.title: Integration: When Bayes Meets Independence
section_4.content: Show how independence simplifies the Likelihood calculation within Bayes' Theorem. Explain that when events are independent, the math simplifies from complex joint distributions to simple products.
section_4.example: A robot sensor: If sensors A and B are independent, the probability of both detecting an obstacle is simply P(A) * P(B), making the Bayesian update much faster.

section_5.title: Summary & Application Loop
section_5.content: Summarize the core takeaway: Independence simplifies computation, while Bayes' Theorem provides the logic for learning from data.
section_5.example: Applying the framework to an email spam filter: Independent keywords (words appearing independently) are used in a Bayesian classifier to label an email as 'Spam' or 'Ham'.

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Independence means knowing B gives no info on A.", "The probability of A remains unchanged by B.", "Visually, the ratio of A is constant throughout."]
        self.setup_layout("The Concept of Independence", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show two coin flip outcomes
        coin1 = Circle(radius=0.5, color=WHITE)
        coin2 = Circle(radius=0.5, color=WHITE)
        label1 = Text("H", font_size=24).move_to(coin1)
        label2 = Text("T", font_size=24).move_to(coin2)
        coins = VGroup(VGroup(coin1, label1), VGroup(coin2, label2)).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(coins, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(coins))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display P(A|B) = P(A) formula
        formula = MathTex("P(A|B)", "=", "P(A)", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'E2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate ratio of A remaining constant despite change in B
        # Represents the constant ratio using a bar chart

        bar_a = Rectangle(height=1, width=3, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.8).align_to(bar_bg, DOWN)
        ratio_viz = VGroup(bar_bg, bar_a)
        self.place_at_grid(ratio_viz, 'C5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(Create(ratio_viz))
        # "Change" in B visually represented by shifting colors/movement
        self.play(bar_a.animate.set_color(GREEN), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Independence means knowing B gives no info on A.", "The probability of A remains unchanged by B.", "Visually, the ratio of A is constant throughout."]
        self.setup_layout("The Concept of Independence", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show two coin flip outcomes
        coin1 = Circle(radius=0.5, color=WHITE)
        coin2 = Circle(radius=0.5, color=WHITE)
        label1 = Text("H", font_size=24).move_to(coin1)
        label2 = Text("T", font_size=24).move_to(coin2)
        coins = VGroup(VGroup(coin1, label1), VGroup(coin2, label2)).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(coins, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(coins))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Warm-up: Conditional Probability", [

        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF9900")
